correspondence: lean/docs/161.md (SHA-256 a1da28a997a9a27c) names as its accompanying paper(s) “A counterexample to Sidorenko's conjecture”, lists the comparator statement lean/ComparatorChallenges/SidorenkoCounterexample.lean (SHA-256 489688f5c4eb60c6) for “Counterexample to Sidorenko's conjecture”, and says: “Sidorenko's conjecture predicts that every bipartite graph $H$ has homomorphism density at least the host graph's edge density raised to $|E(H)|$. The formalization disproves this for the paper's fixed bipartite graph with $35$ vertices and $66$ edges: it constructs a nonempty finite simple host graph with $t(H,G)<t(K_2,G)^{66}$. The separate forcing-conjecture consequence in the paper is outside this statement.” Quoted, not judged: AMVO has not compared this Lean statement with the family's claims or with the manuscripts.
exact_statement:
theorem main : ∃ size : ℕ, 0 < size ∧ ∃ host : SimpleGraph (Fin size),
    (∃ left right, host.Adj left right) ∧ homDensity H host < (edgeDensity host) ^ 66
